Definition: of Hebrew origin (H347); Job (i.e. Ijob), a patriarch:--Job.
BiblicalUsage: Job is named once in the New Testament, and James names him for his patience. In James 5:11 he writes, ye have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the end of the Lord, that the Lord is very pitiful, and of tender mercy.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that one verse is the whole book in a sentence: Job suffered, Job waited, and the end of the Lord was mercy.
